title: Remote Targets and Fleet Boundary
objective: Extend observation/governance to remote development environments without weakening local authority or OSS boundaries.

stories.title: Remote target abstraction
stories.outcome: Model SSH/dev-container/CI-runner targets as explicit machines with independent capabilities and trust.
acceptance_criteria: Remote inventory never masquerades as local state.
Disconnected targets preserve last-seen state as stale, not current.

stories.title: Local-agent remote execution boundary
stories.outcome: Keep mutation execution on the target node under its local safety kernel even when a remote controller requests policy evaluation.
acceptance_criteria: Remote control cannot bypass target safety invariants.
Every remote request is authenticated, authorized, and audit-linked.

stories.title: OSS/commercial protocol boundary
stories.outcome: Define an open local node protocol and separate optional fleet-control services without reducing local functionality.
acceptance_criteria: Single-machine workflows remain fully functional without account/cloud.
Commercial services add coordination, not local destructive capabilities.
